title: Field Oncall Diary — Slow-roll Handoff & Escalation Threads (Aug 2028)
content:
Summary:
This is a compact field-oncall diary capturing a quieter-than-usual week for slow-roll handoffs. Not all installs saw high-severity fires — most work was operational friction: cert handshakes, MTU mismatches in one site, and a recurring NTP drift on two clusters. The diary is intentionally conversational; capture for follow-ups and playbook updates.

Quick highlights:
- Customer: SatoriHealth — slow network path discovered (MTU 9000 mismatch) caused periodic gRPC truncation during model syncs. Workaround: force jumbo frames off for agent until infra fixes.
- Customer: AtlasRetail — KMS policy change blocked bootstrap; incident reopened then escalated to infra-svc. Root cause: least-privilege policy removed kms:Encrypt for provisioning principal.
- Two onprem clusters (NA-west) surface intermittent time skew (~6-12s). NTP servers behind load-balancer were returning stale responses. Added fallback to pool.ntp.org; still monitoring.

Daily notes / standup snippets (Aug 13–16):
2028-08-13 Mon — morning standup (quick)
- Oncall: Priya; backup: Ethan.
- SatoriHealth: net-sig trace attached to DEP-8342; customer-side switch config mismatched MTU. Action: Samir to confirm switch model and push request to customer's network ops for MTU change or accept MTU clamp on host. (ETA: 48h)
- AtlasRetail: provisioning failed during reserved-node attach. María diagnosed missing KMS permission; temporary bypass created with scoped token. Action: María to coordinate with CS to rotate scoped token after infra fix.
- Note: added 'mtu-clamp-flag' to agent (w/ feature toggle) — PR 412 open, needs one more review (Ava).

2028-08-14 Tue — midweek sync
- Follow-ups: Samir confirmed Satori switch is Broadcom Tomahawk (firmware 7.1), customer hesitant to change network config during business hours. Agreed to keep clamp and schedule maintenance window.
- NTP drift: observed at 03:22 UTC on two NA-west clusters; drift spikes correlated with scheduled snapshots causing load on mgmt NIC and delaying NTP responses. Mitigation: deprioritize snapshot job by 10s during NTP sync window. Action: Ethan to update cron in orchestration (DEP-8401).
- Observability gap: agent logs masked the TLS handshake error code when cert chain had intermediate missing. Need clearer error surface for onprem troubleshooting. Action: Priya to file observability ticket and add log sample to Confluence.

2028-08-15 Wed — handoff dry-run + customer comms
- Handoff dry-run for SatoriHealth scheduled at 02:00 PST. Dry-run succeeded with clamp flag. Customer asked for post-migration verification checklist. Quick checklist drafted by Samir and posted to #field-install.
- AtlasRetail: infra-svc rolled permission fix; Maria validated provisioning flow but observed a leftover secret with incorrect KMS ARN (legacy). Action: Maria + CS to delete legacy secret (manual) and redeploy; CS to confirm rotation.
- Patch for agent (PR 412) merged to staging. Performance note: enabling clamp increased avg tail latency by ~12ms during model syncs — acceptable for now but document as tradeoff.

2028-08-16 Thu — escalation grooming + retrospective notes
- Escalation grooming: we formalized an escalation rung for early KMS errors (bootstrap stage) — now triggers a high-prio Slack alert to infra-svc and owner tag. Draft policy in Confluence: /private-deploys/hand-off-playbook#kms-escalation.
- Retrospective highlights: slow-roll handoffs reduce blast radius but increase context-switching overhead. Proposal: create a 1-page 'rehearsal' checklist for customers that prefer non-disruptive maintenance windows (template in Confluence). Action: Priya to own draft.

Open blockers and status:
- DEP-8342 (SatoriHealth MTU): mitigation in place (mtu-clamp). Customer ops scheduling change for switch during weekend maintenance. Owner: Samir.
- DEP-8399 (AtlasRetail bootstrap/KMS): fixed by infra, follow-up to remove legacy secret. Owner: María.
- DEP-8401 (NTP/crontab tweak): owner Ethan; low-risk change queued.
- Observability ticket (OBS-219): capture full TLS chain-related error and surfacing detail in agent logs. Owner: Priya.

Unresolved questions / notes to self:
- Should we expose agent 'safe-clamp' toggle in Console UI for Dedicated/Private customers? Pros: faster recovery for network oddities. Cons: risk hiding misconfigured networks. Need PM input.
- How to better surface KMS misconfigurations earlier? Current bootstrap retries mask the KMS denial as generic 'provisioning failed'. Idea: add explicit KMS permission check early in provisioning flow with precise error mapping.
- Consider adding an automated 'post-handoff verification' ping (small inference request suite) that runs after any network-related config change. Quick win, low risk.

Actions (concrete) — owner / ETA:
- Samir: coordinate with Satori network ops for maintenance window (ETA: 2028-08-19).
- María: delete legacy secret for AtlasRetail and confirm rotated secret exists (ETA: 2028-08-17).
- Ethan: update orchestration cron snapshot delay to remove NTP contention; deploy to NA-west (ETA: 2028-08-18).
- Priya: open OBS-219 with log examples + Confluence doc draft for 'rehearsal checklist' (ETA: 2028-08-20).
- Ava: finish agent PR review and sign off for production rollout (ETA: 2028-08-16).

Slack/Threads/Useful refs:
- Slack: #field-install (thread: "Satori MTU trace")
- Jira: DEP-8342, DEP-8399, DEP-8401
- Confluence: private-deploys/hand-off-playbook (draft section for kms escalation and rehearsal checklist)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy/pull/412 (mtu-clamp feature toggle)

Misc notes (informal):
- Customer sentiment: both SatoriHealth and AtlasRetail appreciated the slow-roll approach — they feel less exposed to risk, even with slightly longer time-to-resolution.
- Oncall ergonomics: quieter weeks are deceptive — good to lock in small improvements (logging tweaks, checklist templates) while load is manageable.
- FYI: I left a short HOWTO in Confluence on adding mtuchange telemetry to agent (very small instrumentation). Could be handy if we see more MTU-related issues as edge boxes proliferate.

End diary entry.
(Notes: will re-open this doc after maintenance windows to capture post-change verification and follow-ups.)
